overall_status: internal theorem and polynomial exact marginal algorithm; no external proof review; novelty unknown

claims.claim: The type-first assignment over completed-gap integer partitions is normalized and full support on binary blocks of fixed horizon.
claims.evidence: RESULT.txt sections 3-4; exact exhaustive check for lengths 1 through 8

claims.claim: For every finite-mean stationary renewal law, pointwise and KL block redundancy are at most log((A_L+1)L), hence O(sqrt(L)).
claims.evidence: Likelihood-ratio proof and partition bound in RESULT.txt section 4

claims.claim: All exact Q_L(prefix) values are computable by a polynomial-time bivariate coefficient DP with polynomial bit lengths; all HJW suffix conditionals for one history share tables and use O(n^3) coefficient/summand updates.
claims.evidence: Generating function and shared marked recurrence in RESULT.txt section 5; exact predictor.py; exhaustive checks through n=8

claims.claim: A fixed-horizon prefix-free code and decoder can encode the class ID, start position, and multiset-permutation rank in polynomial time with less than two bits of overhead over -log2 Q_L.
claims.evidence: block_code.py and the partition/multiset rank-unrank proof in RESULT.txt; all words through L=10 pass check_block_code.py

claims.claim: The HJW suffix-averaging predictor formed from Q_L achieves expected KL risk O(n^-1/2) on the stationary renewal class.
claims.status: proved internally conditional on the cited HJW Proposition 1 and renewal memory bound
claims.evidence: RESULT.txt section 6; HJW arXiv:2404.15454v1 Proposition 1 and Section 3.4

claims.claim: Exact type-first normalization, prefix formula, coefficient DP, stationary block normalization, and likelihood-ratio inequality pass exhaustive finite checks through block length 8.
The exact assignment and prefix DP are novel or were previously unknown.
claims.evidence: Renewal type coding is classical in Csiszar (1998) and Csiszar-Shields (1996); source audit is bounded and the original CS96 full text was inaccessible

limitations: No external proof review has occurred.
The checker is finite evidence, not an all-horizon proof.
The code is horizon-indexed and is not claimed to be a single horizon-free online code.
The complexity bounds are conservative and unbenchmarked.
No sharp minimax constant is claimed.
